summary: Compare two strings after applying '#' as a backspace.
mainInsight: Build both final strings with a stack (O(n) space), or compare from the end of each string with two pointers and skip counters (O(1) space): count '#' characters and skip that many valid characters before comparing the next real character.

approaches.name: Two pointers from the end
approaches.summary: Skip characters with a backspace counter and compare.

commonMistakes: Not skipping several backspaces in a row
edgeCases: Different lengths with the same result

promptVariants: Why scan from the end for the O(1)-space solution?
options: A '#' deletes what came before it, so a backwards scan can skip it
Backspaces only affect the characters after them
The end of the string is always the shortest part
Scanning backwards sorts the characters on the way
cards.answer: A '#' deletes what came before it, so a backwards scan can skip it
cards.explanation: Going forwards you cannot know if a character will be deleted later.

promptVariants: How does the skip counter work?
cards.answer: On '#' increase the counter; on a normal character with a positive counter decrement the counter and skip it. When a character is found with a zero counter it is a real remaining character; compare it between the two strings (or both pointers are exhausted).
cards.explanation: A '#' on an empty text does nothing.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___
cards.explanation: Two pointers and two counters (a stack version uses O(n)).

promptVariants: Which backspaces apply to an empty string?
options: Yes: both become 'c' since a backspace on empty text is a no-op
No: backspaces are not allowed on an empty text
Yes: both become 'ac' after the backspaces apply
cards.answer: Yes: both become 'c' since a backspace on empty text is a no-op

incorrectOptionExplanations.No: backspaces are not allowed on an emp: They are allowed and have no effect.
